builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB: An Open and Efficient Small Language Model for Fast Conversational Agents
summary: It replaces serving a stock instruction-tuned 4B model (Gemma-4-E4B-it or Qwen3.5-4B) with a further post-trained 4B variant plus a bundled speculative drafter for single-user conversational and tool-use workloads. It costs the extra memory and engineering complexity of loading and maintaining the DFlash drafter alongside the base model, and acceptance-rate tuning for your latency profile. Reported gains are measured at concurrency 1 on RTX/Jetson-class hardware, so speedups can degrade under batched serving, and the 21-benchmark accuracy claim may not transfer to domain-specific tasks without re-evaluation.
rationale: The 2.74x decode-speed claim applies only at concurrency 1 with a specific drafter, so an engineer with a single 24 GB GPU should validate acceptance rates and accuracy on their own voice/edge or chat workload before adopting it over a stock 4B baseline.
technique: Post-trained 4B SLM with DFlash speculative decoding

claims.statement: It replaces serving a stock instruction-tuned 4B model (Gemma-4-E4B-it or Qwen3.5-4B) with a further post-trained 4B variant plus a bundled speculative drafter for single-user conversational and tool-use workloads. It costs the extra memory and engineering complexity of loading and maintaining the DFlash drafter alongside the base model, and acceptance-rate tuning for your latency profile. Reported gains are measured at concurrency 1 on RTX/Jetson-class hardware, so speedups can degrade under batched serving, and the 21-benchmark accuracy claim may not transfer to domain-specific tasks without re-evaluation.

With the DFlash drafter, Bolt E4B reaches 2.74x the per-user decode speed of inference without speculative decoding at concurrency 1, and 1.21x the generation throughput of Gemma-4-E4B-it with MTP at batch size 1; the authors also report the highest average accuracy across 21 benchmarks against Gemma-4-E4B-it and Qwen3.5-4B.
